gitspore tokens

PaletteSpacing scaleSize scaleRadius scaleOpacity scaleInterface coloursStatus coloursAgent coloursTerminal palettesLogo2D plant iconsComponent sizes and spacingBordersShadowsOpacityFonts3D scene: colours3D scene: numbersTypography

Every design value of gitspore. Penpot (gitspore_v01) is the source; apps/web/src/theme/tokens.json is its copy, scene.json holds the 3D values. Change a value in Penpot, dump it, run npm run tokens. Click any value to copy it.

Three layers. Base (cozy-06/base) holds the only raw interface values: palette, spacing, size, radius and opacity scales; space.N and size.N are N × 4 px. Semantic tokens (color.ink, color.panel …) point into base; day and night differ only in which base token they point to. Component tokens exist only where code or a layout rule needs a handle (size.row, size.panel-width, space.layout.edge). Content colours (color.agent.*, color.art.*, color.xterm.*) hold their own values. CSS uses rem for spacing, sizes, radii and font sizes (1rem = 16px), px for borders, shadows and everything terminal; tokens.ts has px numbers.

Tailwind classes exist for semantic colours, kept component handles (h-row, w-panel-width, gap-layout-edge), base radii (rounded-lg, same names and values as Tailwind's), shadows, fonts and typographies, plus bg-terminal-bg and text-terminal-fg. Base spacing, sizes, opacity and the palette have none: Tailwind's own p-4, w-10, opacity-35 are the same values. Content colours have none either; use the CSS variable or tokens. In the Tailwind column *-row means h-row, w-…, bg-… and so on. color.muted and color.accent have no utility because shadcn uses those names: use text-muted-foreground and bg-primary.

CSS / CSS modules
.panel {
  background: var(--color-panel);
  border-radius: var(--radius-xl);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg);
  padding: var(--space-2);
}
.title { font: var(--type-title-panel); }
Tailwind
<div className="bg-panel rounded-xl shadow-lg p-2">
  <h2 className="text-title-panel font-title">Your pots</h2>
  <button className="h-10 px-4 gap-2 rounded-lg bg-primary text-primary-foreground">Open</button>
</div>
React Three Fiber
import { tokens } from "@/theme/tokens";
const t = tokens[mode]; // "day" | "night"
<meshStandardMaterial color={t.color.status.waiting} emissiveIntensity={t.scene.glow} />
xterm.js
import { xtermTheme, typography } from "@/theme/tokens";
const term = new Terminal({
  theme: xtermTheme[windowTerminal], // "light" | "dark", the per-window switch
  fontFamily: typography.mono.terminal.fontFamily,
  fontSize: typography.mono.terminal.fontSize,
  lineHeight: typography.mono.terminal.lineHeight,
});
Mode and per-window terminal
<html class="dark">  <!-- night, set by next-themes; no class = follow the system -->
<div class="terminal-light"> <!-- this window's terminal stays light -->
